place.name: Mercy House entrance hall
place.description: Meltwater drops steadily from the coats along the wall. The entrance hall smells of damp wool, lamp oil and the polish used on the visitors' book stand. One passage leads back to the archive, another to the scullery; the courtyard door knocks softly against its latch. Farther along, the ninth ward remains bolted. place.name: Mercy House courtyard
place.description: Snow collects along the courtyard walls without yet settling in the wheel ruts. A gate lamp turns the falling flakes into brief bright scratches. Behind you Mercy House has too many dark windows; ahead, the road drops toward the square. A narrower way runs beside the wall to Dev's winter garden. A kitchen clang carries into the courtyard and is gone almost before you turn toward it.

place.name: Town square
place.description: The square has emptied before the shops have quite closed. Shutters answer one another across the road, and a horse drinks noisily at the trough beneath the notice board. The Pine Lantern keeps a strip of light under its door. Paths lead toward the chapel, the Das and Rao households, and the Mercy House courtyard; beyond the last lamp the forest road becomes a different shade of black. You remember this crossing from childhood, though the signs above the shops have changed.

place.name: Das household
place.description: The Das parlor is narrow enough that a visitor must turn sideways to let someone pass. Tea has dried in a saucer on the parlor table. Beside the stove stands an ash bucket; across the room, a writing desk has been closed and locked. Everything has the cared-for appearance of objects kept through more winters than their owners expected. The only street door returns to the square.

findings.label: signed shopping note
findings.description: A shopping note has been held flat by the sugar bowl. “Kamala—please collect flour and lamp oil tomorrow. Leave the account in the kitchen tin; I shall settle it after breakfast. S. Das.” The ordinary household hand has a distinctive overwritten lower-case d. A dry ring from the bowl crosses the bottom corner.

findings.label: private letters
findings.description: Two letters are folded inside a plain wrapper. One addresses Leena in Mira’s hand: “I love you. That is the part of this I can write without revising it. Meet me at the chapel tomorrow, before the lamps are lit.” A reply signed Leena refers to their private meeting yesterday and asks that the letters be kept from household gossip.

findings.label: household paper
findings.description: An unused paper offcut lies beside the ash bucket rather than inside it. One edge has been cut square; the other is an irregular tear with a small projecting tooth near the middle. The household stationery block is the same pale shade, but there is no writing on this piece.

findings.label: copybook
findings.description: A draft statement copies Tara’s words but crosses out the sentence about the matron refusing release.

tool_result.observation: The threat sheet and unused offcut have matching torn edges; their fibers continue across the join. This links the two pieces of paper, not a writer. Letter strokes on the threat agree with those on the independently signed shopping note, including the overwritten lower-case d. The signature on the threat itself does not establish authorship.

The household copy omits the original sentence about the matron refusing release. Comparing the two texts alone does not identify the person who made the change. The amended lines in the household copy agree in handwriting with the independently signed shopping note.

place.name: Rao household
place.description: The threshold has been lowered and the study furniture set far apart, leaving a clear passage for a wheelchair. On the workbench, acoustic drawings lie under smooth stones. A correspondence drawer sits closed beneath them. From the courtyard comes the click of a loose gate fastening; the street beyond returns to the square. The wheels have left two parallel tracks in the rug beside the workbench.

findings.label: carbon invoice
findings.description: A duplicate account has left a blue-grey impression on thin paper. “Paid by S. Das. Carrier Nalin. Two grave crates: old cemetery to winter garden. Evening cartage; payment received.” A stable clerk has initialled the charge, and an old pinhole marks the corner where this copy was once attached to another account.

findings.label: ink-stained ledger
findings.description: The working book has absorbed ink through its cloth spine. Its inside cover is signed V. Rao. A replacement list of ninth-ward deaths has no entry for Nera; against the earlier numbering, a marginal instruction reads “remove this entry from the clean copy.” The space has been ruled over rather than torn out.

findings.label: signed maintenance receipt
findings.description: A routine maintenance receipt predates the inquiry. “Speaking-tube repair completed and account settled. Vedant Rao.” Hari countersigned its payment when it was filed. The ordinary writing has narrow letters and a doubled loop on lower-case o.
